sites.name: TYSON VALLEY POWDER FARM

portals.name: St. Louis County parcel layer (ArcGIS; St. Louis County Assessor's Office and GIS Service Center)
portals.note: Service endpoint, not a search page. Layer 0 is STLCO_STC_Parcels_Rev2. The service description says it carries ownership, land use and value. Owner and parcel-id field names were not confirmed. Copyright text: St. Louis County Assessor's Office, St. Louis County GIS Service Center.

facts.summary: St. Louis County bought the land in 1947 (year only, per a secondary history).
facts.authority: Unseen St. Louis (Substack history). Secondary account, not a county record.
facts.reference: Unseen St. Louis, 'How a single animal changed history'
facts.quote: St. Louis County purchased the land in 1947.

facts.summary: Per the same secondary history, the government judged the Powder Farm unnecessary in 1961 and put the land up for sale (year only).
facts.authority: Unseen St. Louis (Substack history). Secondary account.
facts.reference: Unseen St. Louis, 'How a single animal changed history'
facts.quote: the government deemed the Tyson Valley Powder Farm unnecessary and put the land up for sale.

facts.summary: St. Louis County acquired 210 acres in 1955 (year only). The land was part of the Tyson Valley Powder Plant during WWII.
facts.authority: Wikipedia, West Tyson County Park. Secondary.
facts.quote: After the war 210 acres (0.85 km2) were acquired by St. Louis County in 1955.

facts.summary: St. Louis County acquired an additional 410 acres in 1979 (year only).
facts.authority: Wikipedia, West Tyson County Park. Secondary.
facts.quote: In 1979 an additional 410 acres (1.7 km2) were acquired.

facts.summary: Washington University obtained the Tyson property after U.S. Military ordnance storage; the article gives 1963 for this use. Current owner per the same page: Washington University (2,000-acre field station).
facts.quote: Washington University obtained Tyson after it had been used by the U.S. Military for ordnance storage in 1963.

facts.summary: EPA Region 7 release: the site won the first annual national federal facility excellence in site reuse award. The release lists it as a non-NPL awardee. It now hosts the WashU Tyson Research Center's Endangered Wolf Center, Lone Elk Park and a World Bird Sanctuary.
facts.reference: EPA Region 7 release, Tyson Valley Powder Farm wins federal facility site reuse award
facts.quote: hosts the Washington University Tyson Research Center’s Endangered Wolf Center, Lone Elk Park, and a World Bird Sanctuary.

facts.summary: EPA release lists the site as a non-NPL awardee. It describes it as a 2,620-acre facility historically used to support the St. Louis Ordnance Plant.
facts.reference: EPA Region 7 release, Tyson Valley Powder Farm wins federal facility site reuse award
facts.quote: Non-NPL Awardee - Tyson Valley Powder Farm, Eureka, Missouri.

gaps: County assessor page (stlouiscountymo.gov) returned HTTP 403 to the research fetch. Its property search URL is unverified, so owner, value and tax status were not checked from a county record.

Recorder of Deeds search (stlouiscountymo.gov) returned HTTP 403. Deed chain, liens and tax-sale status were not checked. A third-party guide says some county search options need a subscription (not verified).
Tax inquiry (taxpayments.stlouiscountymo.gov) and the county GIS viewer (gis.stlouiscountymo.gov) were named in search results but not opened.
No parcel match was run: atlas_parcel_id is null and no point query was made against the ArcGIS layer.
The 1947, 1955, 1961, 1963 and 1979 transfers come from Wikipedia and a Substack history. No county deed or recording citation was found. Years only; no month or day given.
Acreage conflict: the EPA release describes a 2,620-acre facility; the FUDS record shows 2,569.3 acres. Not reconciled.
A 1946 radioactive-storage record and a 2004 USGS metallic-waste survey appeared only as search snippets. They were not opened and are not cited.
FUDS vs FUSRAP program classification is not confirmed from a primary record. Current cleanup status was not found.

sites.name: CAMP HALE

portals.name: Eagle County Assessor Tax Web (public user login page)
portals.note: Opened: titled Tax Web Login, with a Public User Login section and a Registered Users section. No address or parcel search field was visible without logging in. Not used, since the research did not log in. Parcel 220317100001 was not checked.

facts.summary: Presidential proclamation established the Camp Hale-Continental Divide National Monument. The Forest Service manages the 53,804-acre monument within the White River National Forest.
facts.reference: Fact sheet: President Biden designates Camp Hale-Continental Divide National Monument
facts.quote: The Forest Service will manage the 53,804-acre national monument.

facts.summary: Existing Forest Service laws and policies for grazing permits continue to apply inside the monument.
facts.reference: Fact sheet: President Biden designates Camp Hale-Continental Divide National Monument
facts.quote: Laws, regulations, and policies followed by the Forest Service in issuing and administering grazing permits

facts.summary: USACE Omaha District completed an Inventory Project Report in April 1998. The report marked Camp Hale as eligible for FUDS funding.
facts.authority: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Omaha District (as reported in Army.mil, 2014)
facts.reference: Army.mil: Military munitions remediation at Camp Hale (2014-08-20)
facts.quote: In April 1998, the Omaha District completed an Inventory Project Report.

facts.summary: Two time-critical removal actions occurred in 2001 and 2003 (years only; no month given).
facts.authority: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Omaha District (as reported in Army.mil, 2014)
facts.reference: Army.mil: Military munitions remediation at Camp Hale (2014-08-20)
facts.quote: two time critical removal actions have occurred, in 2001 and 2003.

facts.summary: As of August 2014, the cleanup was in the remedial investigation phase, with a feasibility study to follow. The potentially impacted area had been reduced from 226,000 acres to 101,116 acres. No completion date was given.
facts.authority: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Omaha District (as reported in Army.mil, 2014)
facts.reference: Army.mil: Military munitions remediation at Camp Hale (2014-08-20)
facts.quote: The current cleanup phase involves a remedial investigation.

Clerk and Recorder deed index and Treasurer tax status were not checked. No county recording or tax portal was opened.
The newest cleanup status found is the August 2014 Army.mil article. The CDPHE Camp Hale page returned HTTP 403. No 2024-2026 status was found.
Whether this FUDS property falls inside the monument boundary was not checked.
Search snippets mentioned a 2000 closure of about 1,400 acres at Eagle Park and recent munitions finds. These were not opened and are not cited.

sites.name: BUCKLEY FIELD

facts.summary: Sentinel Colorado article on the Buckley AFB compatible use buffer project. It describes over 1,000 acres around the base and a plan to transfer federal and private land to the City of Aurora. It says the $13.3M grant was informally reported approved but not officially announced, so status was pending at publication. This article covers the active base, not the FUDS record directly.
facts.reference: Sentinel Colorado: Buckley AFB compatible use buffer
facts.quote: transferring ownership of federally owned and private land to the city of Aurora.

facts.summary: EPA news release: two open dump areas of less than one acre total, which were once part of the Buckley Field Arctic Training Center (used for training in 1943-1944). The release says the cleanup was funded under the DERP program for FUDS. It places the dump sites in Echo Lake Mountain Park, not on the Aurora base parcel. The link to this FUDS property is inferred from the Buckley Field name only.
facts.reference: EPA: Historic Buckley Field Arctic Training Center restored through cooperative effort in Echo Lake Mountain Park
facts.quote: using the Defense Environmental Restoration Program for Formerly Used Defense Sites

gaps: The Arapahoe County assessor search URL could not be verified. Search results gave conflicting URLs, and the arapahoeco.gov page returned HTTP 404. No parcel or account lookup was done, and atlas_parcel_id is null.
Clerk and Recorder and Treasurer records were not checked.
A 2011 Senate release on a 146.4-acre contaminated Aurora property returned HTTP 403. It is not cited, and its link to this site is unconfirmed.
No 2025-2026 transfer record was found. Buffer project status after 2015 is not confirmed.
No Omaha District FUDS page for property B08CO0021 was opened. The 64,891-acre FUDS footprint was not checked against the base boundary.
Air Force remediation on the active base (Site 1 groundwater, Site 10) is a separate program and was not researched.
Atlas owners (City of Aurora, Arapahoe County, Colorado State Land Board) were not verified against any record.

sites.name: FRANKFORD ARSENAL

portals.name: Philadelphia property site (phila.gov)
portals.note: Fetched: returned a generic 'Property | phila.gov' page. It did not confirm that this is the OPA property search or whether a free search by address or parcel number is available. The complex is marketed as The Arsenal, 2275 Bridge Street, and is split across many parcels and buildings.

facts.summary: Sen. Bob Casey planned to urge the Army Corps to complete the cleanup as a $90M retail megaplex was planned. The developer's group found oil pockets while building. The 1983 deed reportedly promised full remediation.
facts.reference: WHYY: Residual pollution stalls redevelopment of Frankford Arsenal site (2012-11-19)
facts.quote: write to the Army Corps of Engineers urging them to complete the cleanup.

facts.summary: City council committees backed a bill to acquire up to 30 acres on two parcels owned by the PA Fish & Boat Commission, passing 10 acres to PAID, with industrial reuse recommended. Enactment was not verified.
facts.authority: WHYY/PlanPhilly news article (Philadelphia City Council legislation)
facts.reference: WHYY: Council committees recommend industrial use for former Frankford Arsenal (2014-05-14)
facts.quote: acquire up to thirty acres of land on two parcels owned by the Pennsylvania Fish & Boat Commission.

facts.summary: PIDC bought about 40 acres on and near the arsenal for roughly $12 million. Dietz & Watson paid roughly $6 million to PIDC for 22 acres to expand its HQ. The parcel was partly owned by Hankin Management, the City, and the Fish & Boat Commission.
facts.reference: WHYY: With Dietz & Watson transaction, city looks to kickstart reindustrialization (2014-07-01)
facts.quote: PIDC buys 40 acres of property on and near the Frankford Arsenal for roughly $12 million

facts.summary: As reported by Hoodline, lawsuits accuse PAID and Hankin Management of disregarding records and Army Corps findings that pointed to lingering radioactive and chemical contamination. The article also reports glioblastoma diagnoses (attributed to NBC News, not opened). These are allegations. The article notes that proving an environmental cause is difficult. The Hoodline byline shows an AI-assisted icon.
facts.authority: Hoodline (news site, AI-assisted per byline icon). Secondary.
facts.reference: Hoodline: Cancer cluster panic at Frankford Arsenal (2026-07-23)
facts.quote: The complaints accuse the Philadelphia Authority for Industrial Development and Hankin Management Company

gaps: The Pennsylvania DEP FUDS appendix (FY24) returned as an unreadable PDF. The Frankford Arsenal entry and its DOD cooperative-agreement status are unverified.

No Army Corps Philadelphia District FUDS page was opened. Current cleanup phase and decision documents were not checked. A 2015 presentation (search snippet only) mentions a no-further-action decision for Area I soils, but it is not cited.
